newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki recoups loss to end up, U.S. data help.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki recoups loss to end up, U.S. data help.

text.p: Shares ended higher in sturdy volume on Wednesday, rebounding from a weak, thin start as sentiment got a late boost from U.S. producer price data seen as a low-inflation signal, brokers said.
"This is looking more positive all the time ... I think we'll rise tomorrow," one market analyst said after U.S. April PPI fell and Wall Street opened higher.
The HEX index rose 0.7 percent at 3,032.46 after opening easier at 3,003.86, with volume mounting late on to total 675 million markka, over a quarter of it in Nokia.

Nokia's A share gained 1.00 markka to end at 333.50. With Nokia opening higher in the U.S., brokers said the focus was whether it would find a foothold above $65 -- a critical level it breached in early Wall St.

Forestries rose in hefty volume, with UPM-Kymmene ending 1.00 markka higher at 122.50 ahead of its Q1 report before Thursday's open, while Enso closed 0.30 markka higher at 46.60 and Metsa-Serla climbed 1.30 to 41.50.
Heavy trade in Enso stemmed mainly from a 1.8 million block deal brokered in-house at Evli Securities at 46.40 per share.
Brokers said forestries were helped by overnight gains in U.S. paper industry stocks and by this week's news of lower Norscan pulp inventories.
Raisio, still volatile, pared recent sharp losses to end up 12.00 markka at 396.00 in lively 40 million markka trade.
Late in the session, Raisio said plans to launch its patented cholesterol-cutting margarine Benecol in Sweden this year were still on track, with no reason to expect a setback.
Brokers say a large chunk of Raisio stock is believed to be up for sale as operators seek to unlock profits.
